title: Introduce a circuit-breaker layer and region-aware fallbacks for reranker
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: The reranking endpoint is increasingly a single point of failure for high-throughput search and recommendation flows. We observe cascading latency spikes when upstream embedding encoders slow or when regional capacity is constrained. Current mitigations (simple retries and a global timeout) are insufficient: they either amplify load or cause wasted compute and poor tail latency.

Goal: Implement a lightweight circuit-breaker layer plus region-aware fallback policy and graceful degraded scoring path for rerank requests. The circuit-breaker should prevent retries from magnifying outages, reduce wasted token cost, and enable faster failover to cheaper/compatible fallback models or cached scores. Region-aware routing should prefer local healthy pools but fail over to nearest-healthy region with deterministic fallbacks. Success metrics: reduce 95th/99th percentile latency during noisy events by >=30%, cut wasted token cost from retry storms by >=40%, and reduce customer-facing error rate for rerank flows by >=50% in simulated outage scenarios.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of reranker model; trial of new ranking architectures; global load balancing or placement optimizations outside the routing/fallback decision layer.
acceptance_criteria: A circuit-breaker component is added to the rerank front-door that tracks recent error and latency signals per region and per model variant
Default policy trips after configurable failure+latency threshold (e.g. >5 errors or p95 latency > 1.2s in 1m window) and prevents retries for a configurable cool-down period
When tripped, requests are routed to: 1) local cached top-N if available, 2) compatible lower-cost model variant in-region, 3) nearest healthy region according to routing policy
Fallback model path must preserve deterministic ranking ordering semantics and be annotated in response metadata for observability
Integration tests simulate regional failure and show error rate reduced by >=50% and token cost of retries reduced by >=40% compared to baseline
Dashboard panels exist showing per-region CB state, trip reasons, fallback usage, and cost delta; alerts created for unexpected fallback rates
implementation_notes: Add CB state machine as in-memory ring + Redis persistence for cross-process visibility (short TTL snapshots)
Emit events to existing console tracing: rerank.request -> rerank.cb_check -> rerank.cb_trip -> rerank.fallback.{cache|variant|region}
Policy evaluation order: health checks -> latency windows -> error windows -> capacity signals -> config overrides (customer pinning)
Fallback model catalog: tag compatible variants by accuracy profile and token cost; use quantized variants if accuracy delta <= configured threshold
Introduce a degraded scoring path that uses prefix-KV caching + shallow candidate scoring to return good-enough results within 200ms when model fallbacks are unavailable
Ensure deterministic tie-breaking when switching models so downstream clients can diff results and A/B tooling can attribute regressions
progress_updates: 2025-01-16: Spike completed - prototyped CB state transitions and in-process trip logic; validated local trip prevents 3rd retry and reduces tokens in synthetic retry storms (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2410)

2025-01-21: Design review with PM and Console team - agreed on event taxonomy and dashboard widgets; added requirement to annotate responses with fallback_reason header (design doc: drive.redwood.com/rerank-cb-design-v1)
2025-01-28: Implemented initial Redis snapshot writer and p95 latency window aggregator; integration tests added for single-region trip behavior (PR: github.com/redwood/reranker/pull/1083)

2025-02-02: Implemented region-aware routing policy prototype; ran chaos simulation with capacity drop in us-west and observed fallbacks to us-east; still seeing ~12% request amplification due to simultaneous retries - need backoff coordination
review_feedback: PM (Sofia Martinez): Ensure SLOs explicitly include fallback-path latency, and expose per-customer thresholds
Design (Marco Alvarez): Fallback metadata must include model_variant_id and deterministic seed to help reproduce results in the console
Security (Priya Reddy): Confirm Redis snapshots don't leak customer PII and that fallback annotations respect privacy settings
Infra (Ethan Park): Prefer expiring KV snapshots in regional Redis clusters rather than global store to reduce cross-region TTL skews
test_plan: Unit tests for CB state transitions, cooldown, and recovery behaviors
Integration tests simulating: high-latency model, model error spikes, regional capacity drops, and cross-region failover
Load test: 2x normal qps with synthetic retry storms to assert token cost reduction and lack of cascading failures
Canary rollout to 5% of rerank traffic with detailed tracing and rollback automations
Evaluation: run existing rerank quality evals on fallback model variants to ensure quality degradation within acceptable bounds
risks: Risk of subtle ranking divergence when fallback models have different tokenizer or preproc; mitigated by normalization layer
Potential for cross-region latency increase when fallback to remote region is used frequently; must cap remote fallback rate per-customer
Complexity of multi-signal policies could make tuning brittle; will provide sane defaults and feature flags for experiments
Observability gaps early could hide trips; dashboard panels and alerts are a hard requirement before wide rollout
